verses.1: Then Jesus was taken away into the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tempted by the devil.
verses.2: And after fasting for forty days and forty nights, he began to eat again.
verses.3: And when the experimenter came forward, he said to him, “If you are indeed a son of God, then let these stones become bread.”
verses.4: And the one who answered said, “It is written that man shall not live only on bread alone, but must also walk through every place by the word of God.”
verses.5: Then, the Devil took him to the holy city. He placed him on the roof of the temple.
verses.6: And he said to him, “If you are indeed the son of God, then throw yourself down. For it is written that the angels will carry you away along with them, and they will hold you by your hands, even if you try to break your foot against a stone.”
verses.7: Jesus said to him, “It will be written again. You will not try to test the Lord your God.”
verses.8: Once again, the devil takes him to a very high mountain. There, he shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
verses.9: And he said to him, “I will give you all these things, if you only worship me when you fall.”
verses.10: Then Jesus said to him, “Get away, Satan! For it is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him only.’”
verses.11: Then the Devil came to him. And behold, angels also came and stood around him.
verses.12: When he heard that John had been sent out into Galilee, he went there immediately.
verses.13: And after leaving Nazara, he went to Kapharnaoum, on the coastal region near Zabul and Neftalim.
verses.14: So that what was owed by Esaias, the prophet, can be paid off.
verses.15: Land of Zebulon and land of Neftali, a road across the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
verses.16: The people who were sitting in the darkness saw a great light. For those who were sitting in the fields and in the shadows, it was also a light of death that shone upon them.
verses.17: From that time on, Jesus began to preach and say, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.”
verses.18: As they were sailing along the coast of Galilee, they saw two brothers: Simon, who was also called Peter, and Andrew, his brother. They were fishermen, and they threw a net into the sea.
verses.19: And he said to them, “Come back to me, and I will make you sailors of men.”
verses.20: And those who immediately destroyed the networks followed him.
verses.21: And as he moved along there, he saw two other brothers: Jacob, the son of Zebedaeus, and John, his brother. They were on the ship, working alongside their father Zebedaeus to build their networks. He called them by their names.
verses.22: And those who immediately abandoned the ship and their father, followed him.
verses.23: And he went throughout all of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom of God. He also healed all kinds of diseases and weaknesses among the people.
verses.24: And his voice spread throughout all of Syria. He cured all those who suffered from various diseases and illnesses, those who were constantly in pain, those who were possessed by demons, and those who were weak and helpless. He healed them all.
verses.25: And many crowds followed him from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan River.
